S3.01.needs: an existing account with a password or email code
S3.01.note: The same screen serves /login and /signup. Provider and passkey buttons appear above the email field when configured.
steps: Sign out, or open the app while signed out.
Type your account email in "Email address".
Click "Continue".
Enter your password (or the emailed code) and click "Continue".
Look for the signed-in chat page, which means the session was issued.
S3.01.where: Signed out: "Log in or sign up" screen > "Email address" > "Continue"

S3.02.needs: an email address that has no account yet
S3.02.note: There is no separate "Create account" button in the code. /signup renders the same screen as sign-in.
steps: Open the sign-up address (/signup) or sign out.
Type an email address that has no account in "Email address".
Click "Continue".
Follow the next step, which can be "Create a password".
Look for the account being created and the next step (email confirmation).
S3.02.where: Signed out: "Log in or sign up" screen > "Email address" > "Continue" (use an address with no account)

S3.03.needs: a new email address you can read
S3.03.note: The order of sign-up steps is set by the server response, so the exact screen order is not fixed in the code.
steps: Sign up with an email address that has no account.
Look for the "Check your inbox" screen and the "We sent a code to" line with your address.
Open your email and find the code.
Enter it in "Code" and click "Continue".
Check that the account is usable after the code is accepted.
S3.03.where: Signed out: "Log in or sign up" > new "Email address" > "Continue" > "Check your inbox" screen

S3.04.needs: an email account you can read
S3.04.note: This screen takes emailed codes. Authenticator codes are entered on the "Confirm it is you" screen (S3.14).
steps: Reach the "Check your inbox" screen.
Type a wrong code in "Code" and click "Continue"; look for the error.
Click "Resend code" and look for the "Resend code in" countdown.
Enter the newest emailed code (autofill from the email app is offered by the field) and click "Continue".
Look for the signed-in result.
S3.04.where: "Check your inbox" screen > "Code" field (reach it with "Try another way to sign in" > "Email me a code" when a password is offered)

S3.06.needs: an account with a password and access to its email
steps: Type the email of an account that has a password and click "Continue".
On "Enter your password" click "Forgot password?".
Look for the "Check your inbox" screen with the "We sent a code to" line.
Open the email inbox and look for the reset code.
S3.06.where: "Log in or sign up" > "Email address" > "Continue" > "Enter your password" > "Forgot password?"

S3.07.needs: the reset code from the email
steps: Enter the reset code from the email in "Code" and click "Continue".
On "Set a new password" type a new password in "New password".
Read the rule line about minimum length and breach checks.
Click "Continue".
Look for being signed in after the new password is set.
S3.07.where: "Forgot password?" > "Check your inbox" > "Code" > "Continue" > "Set a new password"

S3.08.note: The provider list comes from AGI_AUTH_PROVIDERS and defaults to Google and GitHub. Microsoft and Apple are also defined.
steps: Sign out and open the sign-in screen.
Look for the provider buttons above "Email address".
Click "Continue with Google" (or GitHub).
Finish the provider sign-in in the provider window.
Look for the signed-in chat page.
S3.08.where: Signed out: "Log in or sign up" screen > "Continue with Google" or "Continue with GitHub" (buttons above the email field)

labels.text: This address belongs to an organization. Taking you to its sign-in

S3.09.needs: an account in an SSO-enabled organization
S3.09.note: No separate SSO button exists in the code. The SSO start is triggered by the email step.
steps: Type an email address of an SSO-enabled organization in "Email address".
Click "Continue".
Look for the message "This address belongs to an organization. Taking you to its sign-in".
Finish the organization sign-in in the browser when asked, then look for the signed-in result.
S3.09.where: Signed out: "Log in or sign up" > "Email address" (an organization address) > "Continue"

labels.text: This address belongs to an organization. Taking you to its sign-in

S3.10.needs: a work email on a verified organization domain
S3.10.note: The domain check runs on the server (apps/web/lib/services/organization-verified-domains.ts); the screen only shows its result.
steps: Type a work email whose domain belongs to a verified organization.
Click "Continue".
Look for the message "This address belongs to an organization. Taking you to its sign-in" and the redirect to the organization sign-in.
S3.10.where: "Log in or sign up" > "Email address" (a work email) > "Continue"; the effect shows as the organization message

S3.11.needs: a signed-in account and a browser or device that supports passkeys
S3.11.note: The menu entry that opens Settings was not found under this exact wording; the Settings title is in packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/common.json.
steps: Sign in, then open Settings.
Click "Security" in the Settings list.
Find the "Passkeys" heading and click "Add a passkey".
Complete the device or browser passkey prompt.
Look for the new passkey listed; click "Rename" or "Remove" on it to check those controls.

labels.text: Sign in with a passkey or security key
Use a passkey or security key

S3.12.needs: a registered passkey on the account and a device that holds it
S3.12.note: The button appears only when the server provider list includes passkey and the browser supports passkeys.
steps: Sign out and open the sign-in screen.
Click "Sign in with a passkey or security key".
Complete the passkey prompt on the device.
Look for the signed-in result without a password or code.
S3.12.where: "Log in or sign up" > "Sign in with a passkey or security key" (above the email field); or "Try another way to sign in" > "Use a passkey or security key"

S3.13.needs: an authenticator app on a phone
S3.13.note: The confirm dialog says the change may also sign out sessions and revoke linked access.
steps: Open Settings, click "Security", find "Authenticator app".
Click "Set up authenticator app" (or "Enable two-factor" in the confirm step).
Scan the QR code with an authenticator app, or use "Copy key".
Type the 6-digit code in "Enter the 6-digit code from the app" and click "Verify and enable".
Look for "Two-factor authentication is now enabled on your account." Then sign out and check that sign-in asks for a code.
S3.13.where: Settings > Security > "Authenticator app" > "Set up authenticator app"

labels.text: Lost the device with your codes?

S3.14.needs: an account with authenticator two-factor on, and its device
steps: Sign in with password on an account that has two-factor on.
Look for the "Confirm it is you" screen.
Enter the code from the authenticator app and click "Continue".
Look for the alternatives such as "Use a backup code" or "Text me a code instead".
Look for "Lost the device with your codes?" as the recovery path.
S3.14.where: Signed out: "Log in or sign up" > "Email address" > "Continue" > password > "Confirm it is you" screen

S3.15.needs: a signed-in account with two-factor on, or the setup flow
S3.15.note: Print uses the browser print path; the code shows a fallback message if printing fails.
steps: Open Settings, click "Security", find "Authenticator app".
Click "Generate new backup codes" and confirm in "Replace your backup codes?".
Look for the "Save your backup codes" section with the codes.
Click "Copy codes", "Download codes" and "Print codes" one at a time and check each result.
Look that the codes are shown only once in this view.
S3.15.where: Settings > Security > "Authenticator app" > "Generate new backup codes" (also shown during "Set up authenticator app")

S3.16.needs: an email address you can be reached at
S3.16.note: The page says a person verifies the account, so the restore is handled after the request. Recovery tickets are in apps/web/lib/support/tickets/recovery.ts.
steps: Reach "Can’t reach this email?" from the password screen.
Look for the "Recover your account" page and pick the reason shown.
Fill in every field and an email address we can reach you at.
Click "Request recovery".
Look for the request-sent confirmation, or the error if a field is missing.
S3.16.where: "Log in or sign up" > "Email address" > "Continue" > "Enter your password" > "Can’t reach this email?" (or "Confirm it is you" > "Lost the device with your codes?") > "Request recovery"

S3.17.needs: a signed-in account and a Google or GitHub account not yet linked
steps: Sign in, open Settings, click "Security".
Find the "Sign-in methods" heading.
Click "Connect" next to Google (or GitHub) and finish the provider sign-in.
Look for the row to say "Connected as" with your provider email.
Click "Disconnect" to see the removal step; do not confirm unless the test needs it.
S3.17.where: Settings > Security > "Sign-in methods" > "Connect" next to Google or GitHub

labels.text: This email already has an account

S3.18.needs: one account email and one unused email
S3.18.note: The copy exists. The combined screen may route an existing address straight to sign-in, so the conflict message may be hard to trigger by hand.
steps: Enter an email address that already has an account and click "Continue".
Look for the message "This email already has an account" and the action "Log in instead".
Enter an email address with no account and click "Continue".
Look for "No account uses this email" and the action "Create an account".
S3.18.where: "Log in or sign up" > "Email address" > "Continue" (error message appears on the screen)

S3.19.needs: an account that has not accepted the current Terms
S3.19.note: The re-prompt after a Terms change is applied on the server (apps/web/lib/server/terms.ts); the tester cannot trigger a new version.
steps: Sign in with an account that has not accepted the current Terms, or create a new account.
Look for the "Finish signing in" screen and the line "Review the details below to continue."
Tick the terms checkbox.
Click "Continue".
Look for the sign-in finishing into the app.
S3.19.where: Finish signing in screen after sign-in or sign-up: "Finish signing in" > checkbox "I agree to the Terms of Service and acknowledge the Privacy Policy." > "Continue"

S3.21.needs: a new account that has not finished onboarding
S3.21.note: The page is /welcome. The name field's label inside Settings > General was not checked.
steps: Sign in with a new account.
On "What should we call you?" clear "Preferred name" and type a name.
Click "Continue", then click "Finish" on the next step.
Look for the name being used by the chat (or check the name in Settings > General).
S3.21.where: After sign-in with an account that has not finished setup: "What should we call you?" > "Preferred name" > "Continue"

labels.text: What do you want to do first?

S3.23.needs: a new account that has not finished onboarding
S3.23.note: Copy conflict: the disclosure says the choice is not saved and only picks suggestions, while the "How this works" list says the work described shapes replies, and Expected says it tailors replies.
steps: On step 1 open "What best describes your work?" and pick an option (default says "Select one").
Click "Continue".
On step 2 pick "Write and debug code" or another option.
Read "This picks the suggestions below and nothing else".
Look at the starter prompts that change with the choice.
S3.23.where: /welcome after sign-in: step 1 "What best describes your work?" (pick from the list); step 2 "What do you want to do first?" (radio options such as "Write and debug code")

S3.24.note: Onboarding has no personalization style step, so only the Settings page is reachable for it.
steps: Open Settings and click "Personalization".
Change a value under "Response style" or "Response length".
Open a chat and send a short question.
Compare the reply style with the setting you chose.
S3.24.where: Settings > Personalization > "Response style" (onboarding asks only for name and work, not style)

S3.26.needs: text or a file exported from another assistant, and a Cloud account with memory available
S3.26.note: The Start import button is disabled when no memory controller is available.
steps: Open Settings, click "Personalization", scroll to "Memory".
Click "Start import".
Pick a source (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot or Other), then "Paste memories" or "Upload file".
Click "Preview" and select the memories to keep.
Click "Import" with the count and look for "Imported N memories from".
S3.26.where: Settings > Personalization > "Memory" > "Import memory from other AI providers" > "Start import"

S3.27.needs: a saved work role and an outside account for the connector
S3.27.note: Suggestions are not shown during onboarding itself; they show in Settings > Connectors and only when a work role is set.
steps: Open Settings and click "Connectors".
Look for the "Suggested for" heading with connector buttons.
Click one suggested connector.
Click its connect action and follow the guided flow.
Look for the connector shown as connected.
S3.27.where: Settings > "Connectors" > "Suggested for" row (appears only when a work role is saved)

labels.text: Get notified when the response is ready.

S3.32.needs: a browser where notification permission is still undecided, and a reply that runs long
S3.32.note: The banner appears only while browser permission is the default and a reply is still running. Whether the Notifications page has a browser permission control was not checked.
steps: Send a message that takes a while to answer.
Wait for the banner "Get notified when the response is ready.".
Click "Enable" and look for the browser permission prompt; or click the close control labelled "Dismiss notification prompt".
Open Settings, click "Notifications", and look at "Reply ready" to change it later.
S3.32.where: Chat page during a long reply: banner "Get notified when the response is ready." with "Enable" and a close control; later change in Settings > Notifications > "Reply ready"

labels.text: What do you want to do first?

S3.35.needs: a new account that has not finished onboarding
S3.35.note: The prompt is passed as a starterPrompt query value and filled into the composer by apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx.
steps: As a new account on step 2, click "How this works" and read the points.
Click one starter prompt (or pick a use case and click "Finish").
Look for the chat page opening with the chosen prompt in the message box.
Check that the prompt is not sent until you press send.
S3.35.where: /welcome step 2: "What do you want to do first?" > "How this works" > a starter prompt, or "Finish"
